messages:
Aditya Rao: trying to lock PRD scope today. key open q: which Optimize recs *must* be gated vs “nice to have” gating? and what’s default enforcement (block vs warn) for GA.

Marissa Cole: +1. we need a clean policy statement for rollout. ideally something like “gating required when X changes, optional when Y” with tier carveouts.

Aditya Rao: current list of optimization types: batching, caching, quantization profile changes, routing tweaks (e.g. switching model variant / region fallback), and maybe decoding params(?) when Optimize touches them.

Aditya Rao: my take: quantization absolutely gated. batching/caching probably gated when it changes output ordering/format risk. routing tweaks?? unclear.

Paula Mendes: from rollout POV: we should avoid a surprise “hard block” across the board on day 1. propose stages: observe-only -> soft-block (override available) -> hard-block.

Ethan Park: enforcement wise (control plane) we can support per-optimization-type rules + per-tenant tier. but we need to keep the matrix sane or we’ll regret it.

Dylan Brooks: UX angle: if we gate too much, Console becomes “everything is blocked” and customers blame Optimize. i’d prefer: gate anything that can change tokens/content. don’t gate purely perf knobs that don’t touch outputs.

Jonas Weber: careful: batching/caching *can* change outputs even if the model weights don’t change. esp with tool calls / structured output where formatting is brittle.

Selene Huang: agree. caching: prefix cache + KV reuse shouldn’t change semantics but we’ve seen edge cases w/ truncation and tokenization boundaries. batching: order-dependent bugs, stream chunking differences, tool call serialization.

Aditya Rao: ok so framing might be “gating required for any proposed config delta with non-zero quality risk.” but we need something implementable.

Ethan Park: implementable version: classify proposals into categories:
- Category A (High risk): quantization profile, model swap/routing variant, decoding param changes.
- Category B (Medium): batching/caching params that change scheduling or cache behavior.
- Category C (Low): purely cost reporting / telemetry / quotas (no gating).
Then gating requirement by category + tier.

Marissa Cole: what’s “default enforcement” in pilot? my preference: A = hard block on fail. B = soft block on fail (override w/ justification). C = no gating.

Paula Mendes: + add special handling for timeouts/outages. if eval runner is down we need a deterministic behavior (block vs allow). SRE is going to ask.

Aditya Rao: yep. for timeouts i was thinking: treat as fail for A, treat as “needs manual approval” for B. but not sure.

Jonas Weber: from methodology side, i’d rather not let B slide through on timeout. batching/caching changes are exactly where we’ll get “it got cheaper but customer saw weird output”.

Dylan Brooks: but if we block B on timeout, Optimize apply becomes flaky. we should at least have “Retry eval” and a clear message.

Selene Huang: compromise: timeout != fail. states: PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE (timeout/insufficient samples). Inconclusive triggers rerun; and policy decides whether to block.

Ethan Park: we can encode that. policy engine can return decision = allow | block | allow_with_override. inputs include eval_status and metrics.

Marissa Cole: ok. for default enforcement for GA: do we want *any* ability for customers to bypass? or only internal override?

Aditya Rao: PRD currently says “override path restricted roles” (enterprise). question is: do we let self-serve / startup tiers override? i lean no.

Paula Mendes: +1 no overrides for self-serve. they’ll abuse it and we’ll lose the point of guardrails.

Jonas Weber: also overrides without a prompt set are dangerous. can we require either (a) Redwood default prompt set coverage for that workload tag, or (b) customer-provided prompt set, before any override even exists?

Aditya Rao: good call. propose:
- if no prompt set coverage, Optimize can still *recommend* but apply is blocked (or “needs prompt set”).
- for enterprise pilot, we can allow override if they acknowledge risk + provide justification.

Ethan Park: scope check: do we need to decide in PRD whether routing tweaks are Category A? because that changes model outputs by definition.

Selene Huang: yes, routing/model variant change should be A. even “compatible” variants drift.

Dylan Brooks: agree. UI copy should make it explicit: “This optimization changes the model execution profile and may change responses.”

Marissa Cole: action item: Aditya update PRD section “When gating is required” with categories + initial mapping:
A: quantization, routing/model variant, decoding params
B: batching/caching
C: non-output-affecting
and initial enforcement:
- A: block on fail/inconclusive, no override except enterprise w/ justification (feature-flagged)
- B: block on fail; inconclusive = retry then allow_with_override for enterprise only
- C: no gating

Aditya Rao: 👍 will update PRD and drop link here for async comments.

Aditya Rao: draft link (wip): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/OPT/Optimize+Quality+Guardrails+PRD#GatingPolicyMatrix

Paula Mendes: please also add rollout stages and default: observe-only for 1-2 weeks in prod (collect pass/fail rates) before any hard blocks.

Ethan Park: + specify that enforcement happens at control plane apply endpoint (not just Console). ppl keep assuming UI-only.

Aditya Rao: noted. i’ll incorporate and ping here once updated.
